MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-13, if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 grade level in the Federal service: Performing in depth operation of terrestrial and satellite broadcast telecommunications systems and infrastructure; Leading teams in integration and maintenance support of broadcast production systems, supervisory experience in providing IT support to broadcast communications systems; Managing division or department supporting telecommunications; broadcast engineering; technical requirements contract/financial management; Managing policy development, administration and engineering over Radio & TV telecommunication and IT operations. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. You must also meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 0391 series: A. Undergraduate or graduate education: Major study -- electrical or electronic engineering, mathematics, physics, public utilities, statistics, computer science, telecommunications management, information systems management, business administration, industrial management, or other fields related to the position to be filled OR other education: Communications/electronics or automatic data processing training in technical institutes or business schools above the high school level or in Armed Forces schools that included advanced instruction in addition to basic courses, may be substituted for general experience on a month-for-month basis. B. Experience in evaluating, analyzing, developing, managing, or improving communications systems, procedures, and requirements that demonstrated knowledge of current developments and trends in communications concepts and technology. Incumbent must hold or be able to obtain an IAM Level I certification within six months of the start of employment and must maintain that certification. Failure to obtain and maintain certification is grounds for removal and immediate Tour Curtailment. INFORMATION FOR OVERSEAS: Overseas tour of duty is projected to be 36 months. - You will be required to sign a transportation agreement. - Incumbent may be subject to the 5-year foreign area limitation according to the DoDI 1400.25-V1230, dated 26 July2012. - Applicants who are currently stationed overseas, must have enough time to meet the initial tour stated above. - Applicants who have returned from an overseas tour, and have not been physically present in the United States (CONUS) or Non foreign area for 2 continuous years, may require a waiver. NOTE: If you have not completed 5 years overseas and return to a CONUS assignment, that time spent overseas counts towards the 5 year limitation, unless you have been in the States for at least 2 continuous years. - Medical Care: Applicants who have family members with special medical needs should ensure that prior to accepting a position overseas their family members' medical needs can be met. Access to care in a military treatment facility may not be available to civilian employees except on a space available basis. Consequently, host nation medical facilities may be the only care available. The availability and level of care at host nation medical facilities will vary by location. - Applicants hired from the Continental United States (CONUS) and their family members (who are US citizens) are required to obtain Official Passports prior to departure to the overseas area. - May be subjected to a variety of environmental conditions typical of the overseas areas in which traveling, to include the potential for exposure to acts of terrorism. - Payment for travel and transportation expenses may be authorized. This includes government paid travel transportation, shipment and temporary storage of household goods, and possibly other entitlements based upon the JTR and agency policy. You may be required to sign a transportation agreement. Most civilian permanent change of station travel entitlements are taxable. - For additional information on the tax impact, please visit: https://www.dfas.mil/civilianemployees/civrelo/Civilian-Moving-Expenses-Tax-Deduction.html - For more information on overseas allowances and benefits, please visit: https://aoprals.state.gov/ In Japan, the Civilian and family medical care is subject DHA Rules and those who apply for this position will need to research out restrictions and issues for their medical needs, their families' medical needs and all other medical limitations before they accept this position. 374th Medical Group - Yokota Air Base > Getting Care > Appointments & Referrals (tricare.mil).

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Media Activity. The incumbent will be responsible for serving as Chief, Technical Operations for the Region, a geographically separated Division of the Technical Operations Directorate. As a senior member of the Directorate, the incumbent provides plans, direction, and organization, and exercises control over technical personnel assigned to the Defense Media Activities Regional AO.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Defense Media Activity (DMA) is a Department of Defense (DoD) Field Activity reporting to the Office of the Assistant to the Secretary of Defense-Public Affairs (OATSD(PA)). DMA is a worldwide media organization employing state-of-the art, emerging multi-media production and distribution technologies, and operating from multiple locations in the United States and overseas, and with deployed combat and contingency forces throughout the world.
MajorDuties: As a Supervisory Telecommunications Specialist at the GS-0391-13 some of your typical work assignments may include: Responsible for directing information technology functions, broadcast engineering functions, maintenance standardization programs, and frequency/circuit management for American Forces Network (AFN) and Defense Media Operations (DMO). Responsible for technical operations, which provide satellite, radio and television services for the AFN programming provided to DoD personnel and their families. Responsible for ensuring that equipment and systems associated with studios, media production, signal distribution, transmitters, and satellite terminals are fully integrated and provide 24/7 broadcast and production operations. Plan and program systems designs, evaluations, standards, and policy development; ensure quality control through performance testing; negotiate with U.S. and foreign communications officials; serve as the contracting officer's technical representative (COTR), and provide engineering advice and recommendations to the AFN regional Command Group. Serve as the region's Technology Leader, responsible for developing a strategic vision for network engineering functions that are tied to the DMA Chief Information and Technology Officer (CITO) and network commander's strategic vision and priorities, and charts a proactive course. Responsible for IT operations, operating the computer network and the fulfillment of IT mission and program requirements for DMA- Regional AOR, consisting of a network component hub site and multiple geographically separated broadcast affiliate stations. Incumbent contributes to and directs the planning, development, testing, and implementation (life cycle management) of IT systems both administrative and broadcast, in support of the DMA-Regional mission. Ensure subordinates adhere to all Information Assurance standards and practices, and complies with current DoD and DMA doctrine for network operation and management. Take proper measures to insure optimum data and device security. Verify that all required Cybersecurity information assurance (INFOSEC) documentation is kept up to date. Evaluate compliance and adherence to ensure all DMA-A NetOps host servers on-site in all environments are always in compliance with DISA and DMA HQ NetOps Information Assurance Vulnerability Alert (IAVA) patches and security policies and procedures. Responsible for the assurance that servers in all environments are properly backed up incrementally on a scheduled basis in case of system or media failure. Confirm coordination of system outages with HQ and customers. Ensure the creation and provision of updates to network diagrams and documentation in support of network operations. Conduct or supervise proof-of-performance RF transmission testing and prepares technical documentation for presentation to government officials of the assigned AO. Ensure conformance with applicable U.S. and host country regulations and standards.

All materials must be submitted by the closing date of the announcement. GRADUATE EDUCATION: One academic year of graduate education is considered to be the number of credits hours that your graduate school has determined to represent one academic year of full-time study. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify for the GS-13 grade level if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience at the GS-12 grade level or equivalent: Perform in depth operation of terrestrial and satellite broadcast telecommunications systems and infrastructure; Lead teams in integration and maintenance support of broadcast production systems, supervisory experience in providing IT support to broadcast communications systems; Manage division or department supporting telecommunications; broadcast engineering; technical requirements contract/financial management; Manage policy development, administration and engineering over Radio & TV telecommunication and IT operations. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. In addition to meeting qualifications, your application package must reflect the applicable experience to meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the selected series. You must also meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 0391 series: A. Undergraduate or graduate education: Major study -- electrical or electronic engineering, mathematics, physics, public utilities, statistics, computer science, telecommunications management, information systems management, business administration, industrial management, or other fields related to the position to be filled OR other education: Communications/electronics or automatic data processing training in technical institutes or business schools above the high school level or in Armed Forces schools that included advanced instruction in addition to basic courses, may be substituted for general experience on a month-for-month basis. B. Experience in evaluating, analyzing, developing, managing, or improving communications systems, procedures, and requirements that demonstrated knowledge of current developments and trends in communications concepts and technology. Incumbent must hold or be able to obtain an IAM Level I certification within six months of the start of employment and must maintain that certification. Failure to obtain and maintain certification is grounds for removal and immediate Tour Curtailment. INFORMATION FOR OVERSEAS: Overseas tour of duty is projected to be 36 months. - You will be required to sign a transportation agreement. - Incumbent may be subject to the 5-year foreign area limitation according to the DoDI 1400.25-V1230, dated 26 July2012. - Applicants who are currently stationed overseas, must have enough time to meet the initial tour stated above. - Applicants who have returned from an overseas tour, and have not been physically present in the United States (CONUS) or Non foreign area for 2 continuous years, may require a waiver. NOTE: If you have not completed 5 years overseas and return to a CONUS assignment, that time spent overseas counts towards the 5 year limitation, unless you have been in the States for at least 2 continuous years. . - Medical Care: Applicants who have family members with special medical needs should ensure that prior to accepting a position overseas their family members' medical needs can be met. Access to care in a military treatment facility may not be available to civilian employees except on a space available basis. Consequently, host nation medical facilities may be the only care available. The availability and level of care at host nation medical facilities will vary by location. This includes government paid travel transportation, shipment and temporary storage of household goods, and possibly other entitlements based upon the JTR and agency policy. You may be required to sign a transportation agreement. Most civilian permanent change of station travel entitlements are taxable. - For additional information on the tax impact, please visit: https://www.dfas.mil/civilianemployees/civrelo/Civilian-Moving-Expenses-Tax-Deduction.html - For more information on overseas allowances and benefits, please visit: https://aoprals.state.gov/

Details.JobSummary: Serve as Chief, Technical Operations for the Region, a geographically separated Division of the Technical Operations Directorate. As a senior member of the Directorate, the incumbent provides plans, direction, and organization, and exercises control over technical personnel assigned to the Defense Media Activities Regional AO.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Defense Media Activity (DMA) is a Department of Defense (DoD) Field Activity reporting to the Office of the Assistant to the Secretary of Defense-Public Affairs (OATSD(PA)). DMA is a worldwide media organization employing state-of-the art, emerging multi-media production and distribution technologies, and operating from multiple locations in the United States and overseas, and with deployed combat and contingency forces throughout the world.
MajorDuties: As a Supervisory Telecommunications Specialist you will be responsible for the following duties: Responsible for directing information technology functions, broadcast engineering functions, maintenance standardization programs, and frequency/circuit management for American Forces Network (AFN) and Defense Media Operations (DMO). Responsible for technical operations, which provide satellite, radio and television services for the AFN programming provided to DoD personnel and their families. Responsible for ensuring that equipment and systems associated with studios, media production, signal distribution, transmitters, and satellite terminals are fully integrated and provide 24/7 broadcast and production operations. Plan and program systems designs, evaluations, standards, and policy development; ensure quality control through performance testing; negotiate with U.S. and foreign communications officials; serve as the contracting officer's technical representative (COTR), and provide engineering advice and recommendations to the AFN regional Command Group. Serve as the region's Technology Leader, responsible for developing a strategic vision for network engineering functions that are tied to the DMA Chief Information and Technology Officer (CITO) and network commander's strategic vision and priorities, and charts a proactive course. Responsible for IT operations, operating the computer network and the fulfillment of IT mission and program requirements for DMA- Regional AOR, consisting of a network component hub site and multiple geographically separated broadcast affiliate stations. Incumbent contributes to and directs the planning, development, testing, and implementation (life cycle management) of IT systems both administrative and broadcast, in support of the DMA-Regional mission. Ensure subordinates adhere to all Information Assurance standards and practices, and complies with current DoD and DMA doctrine for network operation and management. Take proper measures to insure optimum data and device security. Verify that all required Cybersecurity information assurance (INFOSEC) documentation is kept up to date. Evaluate compliance and adherence to ensure all DMA-A NetOps host servers on-site in all environments are always in compliance with DISA and DMA HQ NetOps Information Assurance Vulnerability Alert (IAVA) patches and security policies and procedures. Responsible for the assurance that servers in all environments are properly backed up incrementally on a scheduled basis in case of system or media failure. Confirm coordination of system outages with HQ and customers. Ensure the creation and provision of updates to network diagrams and documentation in support of network operations. Conduct or supervise proof-of-performance RF transmission testing and prepares technical documentation for presentation to government officials of the assigned AO. Ensure conformance with applicable U.S. and host country regulations and standards.
